questions.question: The marked price of 85 items was equal to the cost price of 153 items. The selling price of 104 items was equal to the marked price of 65 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
Given

The marked price of 85 items is the cost price of 153 items

The selling price of 104 items equals the marked price of 65 items

**Formula used:**

Profit percentage = (SP-CP)/(CP) × 100

Calculation

Let the marked price be M, the selling price be S, and the cost price be C.

⇒ MP × 85 = 153 × CP 

⇒ MP/CP = 153 / 85 = 9/5 

⇒ SP × 104 = MP × 65 

⇒ SP/MP = 65 /104 = 5/8 

Solving this we get the ratio = CP : SP : MP = 40:45:72

**∴ Profit percentage = (45-40)/(40)× 100 = 12.5% profit**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells a table at a discount of 20 percent and earns a profit of 30 percent. If he sells the same table at 10 percent discount, then what will be his new profit or loss percent?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the ratio formula: **CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)**

CP / MP = (100 − 20) / (100 + 30) = 80 / 130 = 8 / 13

Let MP = 13 and CP = 8. New **SP = 90% of MP** = 13 × 0.9 = 11.7

New Profit% = [(11.7 − 8) / 8] × 100 = (3.7 / 8) × 100 = 46.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 46.25 percent profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 20%, Initial profit = 30%, Second discount = 10%.

**Formula:** SP = MP × (100 − D)% | Profit% = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebf99e86c4ae7845559885e95252ae9dfa071e07c868a06a5dde3212bf971f9d.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100

⇒ Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130

⇒ Since SP₁ is obtained after 20% discount on **Marked Price (MP)**:

⇒ 130 = MP × (100 − 20) / 100 ⇒ 130 = MP × 0.8

⇒ **MP** = 130 / 0.8 = 162.5

⇒ New discount = 10%, so **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 162.5 × (100 − 10) / 100

⇒ **SP₂** = 162.5 × 0.9 = 146.25

⇒ **New Profit** = SP₂ − CP = 146.25 − 100 = 46.25

⇒ **New Profit%** = (46.25 / 100) × 100 = 46.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 46.25 percent profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

The direct relationship is given by CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 ± P/L%), where D is discount and P/L is profit or loss percentage.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It represents how much the price is increased above the cost price before offering a discount.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁ and d₂ are given, the effective discount is [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100]%.</p

questions.question: A 25% profit is made when a discount of 25% is given on the marked price of an item. When the discount is 35%, what will be the profit? (Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit = 25 %

Discount = 25 %

**Concept Used:**

S.P = C.P + Profit

S.P = M.P – Discount

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the cost price be Rs. 100

⇒ There is a profit of 25 % on the item

⇒ So, Selling price = 100 + 25% of 100

⇒ Selling Price = 100+ (25)/(100) × 100 = 125 Rs.

⇒ Also, S.P = M. P – Discount

⇒ Discount = 25 % of M.P 

⇒ S.P = M.P – 25 % of M.P

⇒ 125 = M.P – frac {25}{100} × M.P

⇒ 125 = (3)/(4) M.P

⇒ M.P = 4 × 125 over 3

⇒ M.P = Rs. (500)/(3)

⇒ Now, there is a discount of 35 % on M.P

⇒ New S.P = M.P – 35 % of M.P

⇒ New S.P = frac{500} {3} - frac {35}{100} × frac {500}{3}=(500)/(3)-(175)/(3)

⇒ New S.P = Rs. (325)/(3) 

⇒ Hence Profit = (325)/(3)-100=(325-300)/(3)=(25)/(3)

⇒ Profit % = 8 (1)/(3) ≈ 8 %

 **Hence we can say that profit percent is equivalent to 8 %**

questions.question: A dozen pairs of gloves of Rs. 180 are available at a discount of 10%. How many pairs of gloves can be bought for Rs. 54?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Discounted Price** of 12 pairs = 180 − (10% of 180) = 180 − 18 = 162.

**Price per pair** = 162 ÷ 12 = 13.5.

**Number of pairs** for Rs. 54 = 54 ÷ 13.5 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** of 12 pairs = Rs. 180, **Discount** = 10%, **Total Amount** = Rs. 54.
Formulas: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Quantity = Total Amount ÷ SP per unit.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be5936b74cc1ac55468d55716b728a7ea1e2aaecb6e578a769da96059e7e8fdb.png] 
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** for 12 pairs = 180 × (90 ÷ 100) = Rs. 162.
⇒ Cost of **1 pair** of gloves = 162 ÷ 12 = Rs. 13.5.
⇒ Pairs bought for Rs. 54 = 54 ÷ 13.5.
⇒ Pairs = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pairs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the MP to find the **Selling Price**.

Unitary Method

Finding the value of a single unit first (price per pair) helps in calculating the quantity for any given total amount.

He gains ₹30.80 on the sale of one article.

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

The selling price = q - q × 28% = 0.72q

According to the concept,

0.72q = p + p × 20%

⇒ 0.72q = 1.2p

⇒ 0.6q = p ....(1)

According to the question,

0.72q = p + 30.80

⇒ 0.72q = 0.6q + 30.80 (From 1)

⇒ 0.12q = 30.80

⇒ q = 30.8/0.12

⇒ q = 770/3

Now, the selling price = 0.72 × 770/3 = ₹184.80

∴ The selling price of the article is ₹184.80.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** Let the Marked price be Rs. 100

He gains 20% on 72

According to the question,

SP = 72 = 12 × 6

questions.question: Shopkeeper A marks up his price for an item at 25% and offers a discount of 15%. The same item is marked at 20% by another shopkeeper B and sold at a discount of 12%. Who gets a better deal in terms of % profit and by what profit percentage he sells that item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Shopkeeper A:

Markup = 25%

Discount = 15%

Shopkeeper B:

Markup = 20%

Discount = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Effective Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 - Discount)

Profit Percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the item be ₹100 for simplicity.

**Shopkeeper A:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup)

MP = 100 × (1 + 0.25)

MP = 125

Selling Price = MP × (1 - Discount)

Selling Price = 125 × (1 - 0.15)

Selling Price = 125 × 0.85

Selling Price = 106.25

Profit = Selling Price - CP

Profit = 106.25 - 100

Profit = 6.25

Profit Percentage = (6.25 / 100) × 100

Profit Percentage = 6.25%

**Shopkeeper B:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup)

MP = 100 × (1 + 0.20)

MP = 120

Selling Price = MP × (1 - Discount)

Selling Price = 120 × (1 - 0.12)

Selling Price = 120 × 0.88

Selling Price = 105.6

Profit = Selling Price - CP

Profit = 105.6 - 100

Profit = 5.6

Profit Percentage = (5.6 / 100) × 100

Profit Percentage = 5.6%

**Comparison:**

Shopkeeper A has a profit percentage of 6.25%.

Shopkeeper B has a profit percentage of 5.6%.

**Shopkeeper A gets a better deal with a profit percentage of 6.25%, compared to Shopkeeper B's profit percentage of 5.6%.**

questions.question: An article was marked at Rs. x and sold at a discount of (x - 40)%. If the customer paid Rs. (x - 32), then find the marked priced of the article
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Test the options to find the **Marked Price (x)** that satisfies the given conditions.

For **x = 80**: Discount % = (80 − 40)% = **40%**.

**Discount Value** = 40% of 80 = (40/100) × 80 = **Rs. 32**.

**Selling Price (SP)** = Marked Price − Discount = 80 − 32 = **Rs. 48**.

Check SP condition: **SP = x − 32** = 80 − 32 = **Rs. 48**. (Condition satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = Rs. x

**Discount Percentage** = (x − 40)%

**Selling Price (SP)** = Rs. (x − 32)

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96b79e3faf3393adc1cee4b90e280e456718401b14a1a939db40827f1d1af398.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (x − 32) = x × [100 − (x − 40)] / 100

⇒ 100 × (x − 32) = x × (100 − x + 40)

⇒ 100x − 3200 = x × (140 − x)

⇒ 100x − 3200 = 140x − x²

⇒ x² − 40x − 3200 = 0

⇒ x² − 80x + 40x − 3200 = 0

⇒ x(x − 80) + 40(x − 80) = 0

⇒ (x − 80)(x + 40) = 0

⇒ x = 80 or x = −40

⇒ Since price cannot be negative, x = **80**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 80.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between SP and MP

The **Selling Price** is obtained by subtracting the **Discount** amount from the **Marked Price**: SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage Formula

The **Discount Percentage** is calculated on the **Marked Price**: Discount % = (Discount / MP) × 100.
